gen-silkscreen-gf-ysabeau-office: Ysabeau Office reads modern and friendly, its curves left open at the ends so each letter breathes. And Silkscreen, a lo-fi display face drawn at a single stroke width, turns pixel-blunt and retro if you shrink it down too far.
gen-silkscreen-gf-ysabeau-sc: Retro and a bit lo-fi, Silkscreen spaces its letters out until you can nearly feel the gaps. Ysabeau SC gives it a modern sans-serif partner, and its gaping c is the quality that stands out most.
gen-silkscreen-gf-zalando-sans: Zalando Sans is approachable and neutral, with curves that stay open at the ends of every round letter. But Silkscreen is the one for loud, blocky display lines, where its bars match its stems, while the plain sans simply does the quiet reading.
gen-silkscreen-gf-zalando-sans-expanded: A lowercase a with no hairlines at all, that is Silkscreen, a retro, lo-fi display face with spaced-out letters. Zalando Sans Expanded follows as a clean plain sans, and Silkscreen earns its keep when it runs big and brief.
gen-silkscreen-gf-zalando-sans-semiexpan: Zalando Sans SemiExpanded brings open-mouthed curves on c, e, and s, modern and polished. Zalando Sans SemiExpanded against Silkscreen, which looks like vinyl cut to one line width, makes the strongest quality here a lo-fi retro bite meeting crisp sans clarity.
gen-silkscreen-gf-zcool-xiaowei: ZCOOL XiaoWei reads clean and modern, with a gentle shift in weight from stem to hairline and no ink pooling in the turns. And Silkscreen, with zero modulation between its strokes, brings the retro, lo-fi edge while the plain sans keeps the paragraphs smooth.
gen-silkscreen-gf-zen-kaku-gothic-antiqu: Silkscreen spaces every letter so widely you can almost feel the air between them, like spaghetti laid out in lines. Zen Kaku Gothic Antique then carries a long passage smoothly, its t crossbar matching the stem and every bend open to the eye.
gen-silkscreen-gf-zen-kaku-gothic-new: Approachable and neutral on the body side, this pairing sets a lo-fi retro display face above a sans with open curves and no hairlines at all. Silkscreen grabs attention; Zen Kaku Gothic New settles in.
gen-silkscreen-gf-zen-maru-gothic: Silkscreen is a lo-fi, retro display face that lays its letters out like spaghetti, each one with room around it. It handles the shouting, but Zen Maru Gothic, a plain sans, handles the following of a single thread.
gen-silkscreen-ibm-plex-sans: Pixel-bright and retro, Silkscreen holds one stroke width throughout, its letters spaced like spaghetti laid out in a line. IBM Plex Sans, technical yet approachable, gives each bowl a wide channel, so nudge its size up a bit.
